messages:
Mike: quick heads-up — new reranker candidate (rdrk-v2) shows offline +0.9% NDCG but prod A/B has -3% MRR on short queries. filing notes here so we don't lose context

Maria: ugh, that's a classic mismatch. did we run the same truncation/candidate splitting as prod?

Mike: good q. offline harness concatenates doc passages into a single scoring string with <DOC> markers (max_total_tokens=1024). prod scoring uses per-passage scoring capped at 256 and relies on prefix KV cache on the serving path.

Sasha: that screams cache/attention layout difference. int8 variants can change token-level attention noise and combined with KV caching you can get rank reorders. did you test fp16 vs int8?

Mike: yes. quick results:
```
# eval command we ran
python eval_rerank.py --model rdrk-v2 --quant int8 --candidate_strategy concat --max_tokens 1024 --holdout=dev_small

# printed snippet
NDCG@10: 0.482 (+0.9 vs baseline)
MRR@10 (offline): 0.354
```
But prod A/B: MRR@10: 0.342 (baseline 0.353) for short queries subset.

Jon: can you paste the prod scoring config? maybe prod has pretokenize/strip-html differences or different whitespace normalization. small queries are sensitive.

Mike: prod config (serving):
```
- per_candidate_max_tokens: 256
- use_prefix_kvcache: true
- tokenizer_normalize: true # strip html, collapse whitespace
- scoring_mode: passage_level
```
Offline harness uses: concat mode and minimal normalization to preserve tokens for debugging.

Maria: two hypotheses: 1) concat gives more context and helps model rerank fp16/int8 differently, 2) KV cache + int8 causes slight scoring drift on short contexts that flips ordering for near-ties.

Sasha: we should repro offline with harness matching prod: per-candidate scoring, same tokenizer flags, and run both fp16/int8 with/without prefix cache emulation. Also test ordering sensitivity by adding tiny random noise to logits to simulate floating jitter.

Mike: started a small experiment run, command below. I'll share logs when done.
```
# match prod harness
python eval_rerank.py --model rdrk-v2 --quant int8 --candidate_strategy per_passage --per_candidate_max_tokens 256 --tokenizer_strip_html --use_prefix_cache_emulation true --holdout=dev_small --seed=42
```

eval-bot: queued job id=job_2026_03_21_99 (estimated 45m)

Jon: while that's running, can we sanity-check the candidate order input to prod vs offline? if offline shuffles or dedupes differently that could explain NDCG->MRR differences.

Mike: confirmed: offline keeps original candidate order from oracle file. prod candidate pool comes from retrieval pipeline which applies a light rerank and dedupe that can change order. I exported 200 example requests where ordering differs and will run targeted diffs.

Maria: nice. also run candidate-level scoring without cache to isolate prefix effect. add variant flag `--no_cache` in the experiment.

Sasha: remind me — does our quant rollout use PTQ per-layer calibration or a global scale? layer-wise PTQ reduces per-layer bias, could matter for short contexts.

Mike: PTQ is per-channel symmetric with per-tensor scale for the int8 artifact we used. I can queue a per-layer calibration run if needed.

eval-bot: job_2026_03_21_99 completed. results uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/4207654321/job_2026_03_21_99/metrics.json

Mike: quick summary from that job:
- int8 + per_passage + cache_emulation: NDCG@10: 0.471 (offline)
- int8 + per_passage + no_cache: NDCG@10: 0.474
- fp16 + per_passage + cache_emulation: NDCG@10: 0.475
- short_queries subset MRR: int8+cache 0.338, int8+no_cache 0.345, fp16+cache 0.347

Sasha: looks like cache_emulation hurts int8 more than fp16, consistent with numeric jitter accumulating in KV.

Jon: next steps: 1) re-run prod-like A/B with fp16 rollout for short-query cohort only (fast rollback), 2) queue per-layer PTQ for int8, 3) normalize offline harness to use same tokenizer stripping and retrieval ordering when possible.

Maria: agree. I'm OK rolling fp16 short-cohort to stop immediate regression while we fix int8 flow. @deploy-bot can you schedule a short-cohort canary for fp16?

deploy-bot: scheduling canary: model=rdrk-v2-fp16 cohort=short_queries rollout=10% start=2026-03-21T15:40Z; will auto-rollback if MRR drop > 1% over 30m

Mike: thx. I'll own the PTQ per-layer job and the offline harness fixes (candidate ordering + tokenizer parity). Sasha can you own the KV cache emulation verification in the runtime tests?

Sasha: yep I'll add a unit test in runtime that simulates int8 kv sequences and asserts logits difference < 1e-3 for canonical cases.

Maria: sounds good. please post short postmortem summary in follow-up thread with final decision and metric graphs.

Mike: will do. tl;dr: mismatch between offline concat-harness and prod per-passage + prefix cache amplified int8 numeric drift; short-query MRR sensitive to small reorderings. mitigation: fp16 short-cohort canary + per-layer PTQ + harness parity work. :white_check_mark:
